engagement_title: Fernwood memorial keepsake: bring four eras of family scans to one printable set, rerun the funeral home's card and framed page for the service, and build the memory book so the family can keep changing the captions
vertical: Media, publishing and personal, heritage and memorial commission for a family (Brattleboro, Vermont)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Upwork family history restoration brief in which a private individual digitising roughly twenty four antique 1910 postcard photographs of a touring stage magician company asks for the photographic FRONT and the handwritten BACK of each, delivered legible for a printed memorial book and for sharing with family. Co-anchor: the Freelancer.com posting from an individual with 'several old photo scans' to restore 'for A4 printing to mount on my wall', naming 'color fading', 'scratches or tears' and 'blurriness'. That second conceit is deliberately not taken at face value, because the three damages it names are precisely what this connector cannot do: there is no heal, clone or inpaint to rebuild a torn corner or a scratch crossing photographic texture, and no sharpen for blurriness. The honest fuller commission the same client actually needs is the one built here: the scans brought to one printable house look by tonal and colour means, damage handled by crop, plate scale and placement rather than faked, and the result carried into a keepsake the family can print and keep editing. No real person, family, troupe, venue or trademark is named; the magician company is the fictional Veranda Marvelli Company with a fictional lead Aldo Marvelli, and the Fernwood family, Walter Fernwood and the Allsop and Vance funeral home are invented for this benchmark. Verdict STRENGTHEN: the ledger concept was a restoration pass plus a book, which sat on one surface and promised repairs the tools cannot make.
client_one_liner: My father died in March, the service is in five weeks, and what we have is a shoebox of scans spanning ninety years that do not sit together, a eulogy nobody has laid out, and the press files from my mother's service in 2019 that we would like to use again.
client_brief:
Fernwood family, memorial keepsake

My father, Walter Fernwood, died in March at ninety four. The service is at the Congregational hall in Brattleboro in five weeks and there will be around sixty people, most of them older than me.

We have a shoebox my brother scanned. It spans everything. There are postcard photographs from around 1910 of my grandfather's company, he toured as a stage magician's assistant, and those have handwriting on the back that we want in the book as much as the fronts, because that is his hand. There are studio portraits from the thirties, a run of colour prints from a summer in 1968 that have gone strange and pink, drugstore prints from the nineties and some phone pictures from the last few years.

What we want is a book. Not a photo album, a book: plates with captions, a contents page at the front, and the eulogy my daughter has written laid out properly in the middle of it. Something we would be glad to have on the table at the hall and glad to keep afterwards. We would also like one page on its own that we can frame, and a small card for people to take home.

The funeral home ran the card and the framed page for my mother in 2019 and gave us the files. We would like the same shape of thing so it sits with hers on the shelf. For the cards, each one should carry the name of the person we are handing it to and one line about how they knew him. That list is in a spreadsheet.

Please do not brighten this up. My mother's was done by somebody who made everything cheerful and it was awful. And do not invent anything that is not in the photographs. Some of them are damaged and we would rather see the damage than see it painted over.

We will keep changing the captions until the last minute, so we need to be able to do that ourselves.
price_band_and_audience: Heritage and memorial commission, 300 to 600 dollars, family and mourners aged 45 to 75, most of them reading printed pages rather than screens. The band is load-bearing in both directions. This is not a luxury commemorative volume, so gilt edges, foil rules, full bleed dramatic plates and a designer typographic conceit read as expensive theatre at a Congregational hall and against the mother's 2019 card on the same shelf. Nor is it a discount photo book, so a dense grid of small plates, drop shadows, decorative corners, script headings and a bright cheerful palette cheapen the keepsake and are exactly what the client says was done badly last time. What the money buys at this band is restraint: generous white space, a quiet classical text face at a size a seventy year old reads without glasses, plates given room, captions that are plain, and an unbroken calm from the contents page to the colophon. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the occasion even if every plate is technically clean. A real posting of this shape runs 350 to 900 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A private heritage and memorial keepsake commissioned by a family for a service and to keep afterwards.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Commissioned 2024 by the Fernwood family, Brattleboro, Vermont, for a service of around sixty people at the Congregational hall.
brand_identity.about: This is a family memorial keepsake for Walter Fernwood, who died at ninety four. It is a book, not a photo album: plates with captions, a contents page, and the granddaughter's eulogy laid out in the middle, alongside a framed page and a small card for mourners to take home. The visual voice is set by two things: the family's wish that nothing be brightened or invented, and the funeral home pieces made for Walter's late wife in 2019, which the new work should sit beside on the shelf.
brand_identity.audience: The family and around sixty mourners aged 45 to 75, most of them reading printed pages rather than screens, many of whom remember the people in the photographs.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Heritage and memorial commission, 300 to 600 dollars. Neither a luxury commemorative volume with gilt and foil, nor a discount photo book with grids and script headings. What the money buys is restraint.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet classical text face set large enough for a seventy year old to read without glasses, paired with a modest sans for captions and contents. Generous white space, plates given room, plain captions, one unbroken calm from the contents page to the colophon. No script, no decorative corners.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, gentle, unsentimental. Lets the photographs and the family's own words carry. Example line the book would write: The company toured for eleven seasons, and this is his father's hand on the back of the card. No cheerfulness, no exclamation points.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: There is no brand file. The look is inherited from the funeral home's two 2019 press files (a keepsake card and a framed page) that the family wants matched so the pieces sit together on the shelf, and from the family's own scans, eulogy and typed transcriptions. The funeral home's designer has retired and left only flat press files. Damage in the scans is to be shown honestly, handled by crop and placement rather than painted over.
brand_identity.values: Nothing invented and nothing brightened. Honesty to the photographs as they are, and a keepsake the family can keep editing until the day of the service.

assets_supplied.name: shoebox_scans/ (26 files, mixed 1200 to 4800 px)
assets_supplied.kind: Flatbed and phone scans spanning four eras: 1910 postcard photographs of a touring company with handwriting on the reverse, 1930s studio portraits on mount card, a 1968 colour run, 1990s drugstore prints and recent phone frames.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Everything my brother could scan. Some of them are damaged and we would rather see the damage than see it painted over."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the 1968 colour prints have shifted so far in their dye layers that no correction within reach brings them to the same neutral as the rest without taking the skin green, which is discoverable only by running the correction and looking at the result beside the others. Separately, four scans are photographs of framed prints rather than scans of prints, carrying glass reflection and keystone, and the postcard reverses are pencil on cream card sitting in so narrow a tonal band that the move which makes them legible also greys the card unless it is confined.

assets_supplied.name: keepsake_card_2019_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The funeral home's flat press file for the A6 keepsake card handed to mourners at the 2019 service, fonts embedded, produced from a real page layout. Carries a name line, a relationship line, a date line and a placed photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What they printed for my mother. We would like the same shape of thing so the two sit together on the shelf."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The relationship line sits in a fixed measure frame sized for the two and three word entries the 2019 list happened to hold. Longer entries do not spill and do not error, they simply stop rendering at the frame's last line, so a merged card looks finished and complete at thumbnail while a mourner's line is cut mid phrase at trim. The frame's true capacity depends on the applied face and size the retired designer set, which no readout states.

assets_supplied.name: framed_page_2019_press.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The funeral home's flat press file for the A4 framed memorial page from the 2019 service, with a large plate area, a name and dates, and a short verse block.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The page we framed for my mother. Same size, same place on the wall."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The plate area is a portrait proportion graphic frame while most of the scans worth framing are landscape, and how the merge fits or fills a placed image into that frame, whether it centres and what it clips, appears in no readout and is visible only on the rendered page. The page also carries no bleed and no bleed can be introduced, so any plan that runs a plate to the paper edge is unbuildable.

assets_supplied.name: guest_list.xlsx export
assets_supplied.kind: The family's spreadsheet of people expected at the service, with columns for name, household, relationship line and which side of the family they belong to.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Who is coming, and one line about how they knew him. My sister wrote the lines."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The list runs longer than the number of cards actually needed because several couples appear as two rows sharing one household and one line, and a handful of relationship lines run to a full sentence while most are two words. There is no photograph column at all, so binding a plate per family branch requires a column the family never made, built to the merge's own image column contract with filenames the agent controls.

assets_supplied.name: eulogy.txt and transcriptions.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The granddaughter's eulogy as plain prose with emphasis marked, and the family's own typed transcription of every handwritten postcard reverse.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What my daughter will read, and what the backs of the postcards say. We typed them out because you will not be able to read his hand."

acceptance_bar: The plates sit together as one book when turned page by page: one black point, one sense of warmth, one weight of print. A plate that cannot be brought to the set is treated as its own thing deliberately and said so in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.

Nothing is invented. No damage is painted over, no missing corner is rebuilt, no detail appears that is not in the scan. Where damage cannot be removed it is handled by crop, plate scale or placement, and the note says which.

Nothing is brightened up. The book stays quiet: no cheerful palette, no decorative corners, no script headings, no drop shadows, no full bleed drama. A polished page that reads as celebratory has failed the occasion whatever else is right about it.
The postcard reverses are legible as handwriting on cream card, not as grey handwriting on grey card, and the transcription runs beside each one exactly as the family typed it.

No delivered file exceeds its source scan's pixel dimensions, and no tool's silent resize goes unreported. The 1200 px scans are placed at a size they can actually hold and the note says where that constrained the layout.

Exactly one keepsake card per household attending, not one per row, with no duplicate card for a couple and none missing. If the count shipped is not the count the list implies, the note says which rows were merged and why.
Every keepsake card carries its relationship line in full at trim. A line that stops short at the frame edge is a failed card even if the file opened fine and looked complete.
The framed A4 page is rendered at true print resolution at A4 trim, and the plate on it is placed so the subject is whole rather than cropped by the frame's own fitting.

The book comes back as a native editable document the family can change captions in until the day before, with every plate actually visible in it and every text element carrying its licensed face at that family's own numeric weight.
The book reads as one continuous calm from the contents page to the colophon, at a text size a seventy year old reads without glasses.

A written note: the treatment applied per era with one line on why that era differs, the type and grid basis, what each 2019 press file turned out to be as editable structure, every guest list row questioned and how it was resolved, and every resize any tool reported.

adobe_surfaces.role: Brings four eras to one printable set with a call per scan rather than one batched pass, because a single parameter set that suits a 1930s silver print takes a 1968 colour print further into its cast. Runs confined moves where a whole frame move is wrong, chiefly on the postcard reverses where legibility and the card's own colour pull against each other. Handles damage by crop and placement rather than by invention, carries the era level treatment decision, and cuts every plate to the proportion the layout actually needs at native scale.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml (on both press files, then again to audit each prepared template), generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as generator and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (application/x-indesign and application/pdf, additionalImageFiles, recordRange), document_render_layout (resolution 300, createSeparateFiles, pageRange in N-N form)

The funeral home's flat press files become live merge templates with no working file to start from, the guest list becomes the data source, and the run produces the keepsake cards one per household at trim plus the framed A4 page at true print resolution. This is the only surface here that does record per page variable data, and the true story text must be reconstructed from the exported interchange file rather than trusted from a convenience readout.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable belongs to which surface: the keepsake card and the framed page to the merge surface because they are record per page against layouts the family wants matched, the book and the share card to authored fixed canvases because captions change until the last minute, the scans to imaging.
trajectory.judgement: Authoring the card from scratch loses the match with the mother's 2019 pieces that the family asked for. Trying to merge the book finds that record per page cannot produce a contents page, a eulogy spread and a square share card in one document.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the twenty six scans, both 2019 press files, the guest list, the eulogy and the transcriptions, holding every returned presigned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by era and by whether a file is a front or a reverse, because a postcard front and its reverse must stay paired through thirty later operations.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by era, subject and front or reverse.

trajectory.action: Preview every scan and triage: era, medium, native pixel scale, whether the file is a scan of a print or a photograph of a framed print, whether the damage sits inside the picture or in the margin, and which fronts pair with which reverses.
trajectory.judgement: The family says damaged; the useful distinction is whether damage sits in the picture, where nothing lawful can remove it, or in the margin, where a crop can. Native scale decides which plates can print large and which must be small, and that decision governs the whole book grid.
trajectory.produces: A per scan triage note: era, medium, native scale, damage location, pairing, and whether the file is a scan or a photograph of a frame.

trajectory.action: Straighten and square the scans that went through the flatbed crooked, before any crop or plate size is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, and the 1200 px scans have the least to spare and are already the ones constraining plate size.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, with the pixel cost recorded per file.

trajectory.action: Set the house target off the strongest mid era print and correct each scan toward it with its own call, logging the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a book, not twenty six good pictures. One black point and one sense of warmth across ninety years of media is the whole commission, and a scan made individually pleasing is a scan that will not turn with its neighbours.
trajectory.produces: Corrected masters at source scale with a per scan parameter log.

trajectory.action: Treat the postcard reverses as their own problem: bring pencil on cream card up to legibility with the move confined to the writing rather than applied to the whole card.
trajectory.judgement: A whole frame move that makes the pencil readable takes the cream card grey, which turns his hand into a photocopy. Prompt wording is the gate, and naming the card pulls the selection to the card while naming the writing's own character pulls it to the writing.
trajectory.produces: Legible reverses that still read as cream card, paired to their fronts.

trajectory.action: Bring the colour eras toward the house neutral, working the 1968 run and the 1990s drugstore prints against the same target as the monochrome eras.
trajectory.judgement: A colour cast and a dye shift are not the same failure and do not answer to the same instrument, and how far a shifted emulsion can be moved before the skin goes wrong is a property of that print rather than a setting.
trajectory.produces: Colour era plates carried as far toward the house target as each will go, with the parameters recorded.

trajectory.action: Cut every plate to the proportion the book grid and the framed page actually need, removing margin damage where the damage is in the margin, at native scale, reading every tradeoff record.
trajectory.judgement: A crop is the only lawful remedy for a torn margin and it costs picture. Where the damage is inside the picture the plate is placed rather than cut, which is a layout decision made here rather than later.
trajectory.produces: Plates at final proportions with the tradeoff records captured and the constrained files flagged.

trajectory.action: Search short generic queries for one quiet cover frame, exclude generative tech candidates, license and download it at full resolution. Create the family board and place the plate shortlist so three households can agree on the selection.
trajectory.judgement: Restraint rather than beauty: the cover frame has to disappear behind the name, and a frame that is doing anything is the wrong frame. The board is the only way three households in three states settle a selection without another five rounds of email.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale cover frame and a persistent shareable board carrying the shortlist with a verified item count.

trajectory.action: Convert both 2019 press files to native documents, export the interchange file from each, and read what each exposes: text frames, graphic frames with their integer item ids, bounds, applied faces and sizes, and the true story text reconstructed from the concatenated content runs.
trajectory.judgement: A convenience readout of a story is not the story, and offsets computed from it are internally consistent and wrong. The graphic frame's bounds are also the first hard fact about what proportion of plate the framed page can actually carry.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory per press file and the reconstructed story text for each.

trajectory.action: Normalise the guest list into one row per card actually needed, resolving couples sharing a household onto one card, and build the plate column the family never made, to the merge's own image column contract with filenames the agent controls.
trajectory.judgement: Which rows collapse into one card is the family's convention rather than a data rule, so the agent proposes and records rather than silently deciding. The relationship lines are the sister's words and may be neither reworded nor shortened.
trajectory.produces: A normalised data source plus a written list of every row questioned and how it was resolved.

trajectory.action: Build the field mapping for both templates against the reconstructed story text, validate it, prepare each merge template, then export the interchange file again from each prepared template and search it for every expected placeholder before merging anything.
trajectory.judgement: A success message is not verification. The only evidence a placeholder exists is finding it in the prepared document's own stories.
trajectory.produces: Two prepared merge templates with every field confirmed present by inspection.

trajectory.action: Merge to native documents and render: the keepsake cards one per household at A6 trim, and the framed page as a single record at A4 and true print resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Identity is established by opening each file and reading it, not by the order a list of links came back in, and print resolution has to be produced by the render step rather than requested at merge time.
trajectory.produces: The keepsake card run and the framed A4 page at print resolution, each opened and read.

trajectory.action: Call the recommender once per typographic role, read the real numeric weights from the family style inventory, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit for the book.
trajectory.judgement: The recommender refuses to pair, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction, judged by mourners aged 45 to 75 reading a printed page rather than by a design audience. A display cut carries its own slug rather than a weight, and a reflexive numeric weight ships a different cut with no warning.
trajectory.produces: A type and grid basis by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, plus one embed kit.

trajectory.action: Author the book as one self contained document: contents page, plate pages pairing each postcard front with its reverse and the family's transcription, single plate pages for the studio and colour eras, the eulogy spread with its emphasis carried as real inline runs, a colophon, and the square share card at its own canvas size.
trajectory.judgement: Every plate must be carried as embedded image data, family and weight declared on the text elements themselves, each root declaring its own canvas size, and the whole thing has to hold one calm from the first page to the last.
trajectory.produces: One authored HTML document carrying the book roots plus the share card root.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then read the returned per root markup for every root and the rendered preview for the first, and reconcile both against what was authored, page by page.
trajectory.judgement: Success is not fidelity and the preview shows the first root only, so every page after the first can be verified only from the returned markup, and a construct that was silently normalised or dropped is visible nowhere else in the entire chain.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document plus a page by page reconciliation of authored intent against returned structure.

trajectory.action: Update the shared board with the final plates, the licensed cover frame and the rendered card and framed page, reading a partial success as partial and re-sending only what failed.
trajectory.judgement: The placement cap per call is real and a partial acceptance is reported as a success, so the count placed has to be checked rather than assumed.
trajectory.produces: A board carrying the final set with a verified item count and nothing silently dropped.

trajectory.action: Write the note: the treatment applied per era with one line on why that era differs and where damage was handled by crop or placement rather than removed, the type and grid basis, what each 2019 press file turned out to be as editable structure, every guest list row questioned and its resolution, and every resize any tool reported.
trajectory.judgement: The family must be able to change captions on their own until the day before the service, and must be told plainly what could not be repaired rather than discovering it in print.
trajectory.produces: The handover note and the source files behind every editable deliverable.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the 1968 run can join the book at all in colour. The correction that brings the rest of the colour era to the house neutral is applied to those prints and reports success, and each one looks better on its own than it did. What only appears when they are laid beside the corrected 1930s and 1990s plates is that the two worst have not arrived: their dye layers have shifted far enough that the move which neutralises the cast takes the skin toward green, and pushing further does not converge because the hue range available is moderate rather than complementary. There is no readout for how far an emulsion will travel; it is a property of that print, and the evidence is the set, not the file.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the only way to learn how far a shifted print will move is to move it and look at it beside the others, and there is no earlier moment at which the answer exists. Nothing states it: the brief says the 1968 prints have gone strange and pink and asks for a book, while the acceptance line about the plates sitting together is the family's own standard rather than a disclosure. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is an era level treatment decision that changes what the book is, not a re-execution of the same plan.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Lay the corrected colour plates beside the corrected monochrome plates and judge them as a book turns them. For the prints that will not come, stop chasing the neutral and take a deliberate decision instead: carry that era as a monochromatic tint keyed to the book's warmth so it reads as its own chapter rather than as a failure, or place the two worst small and late rather than as full plates. Then re-cut those plates to the sizes the new decision implies, and record the choice in the note so the family is told rather than shown.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A memory book in which the summer of 1968, the only colour record of the man's young family, turns up as two pink faced plates among ninety years of otherwise settled pages, handed round a Congregational hall by people who remember that summer.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the cards and the framed page actually carry what they claim. Two things arrive only on the rendered pages. First, the funeral home's relationship line frame is a fixed measure sized for the two and three word entries the 2019 list happened to hold, so the handful of longer lines the sister wrote do not spill and do not error, they simply stop rendering at the frame's last line: the card looks finished, the merge reports success and every file opens. Second, how the merge fits a landscape plate into the framed page's portrait graphic frame, whether it centres and what it clips, appears in no readout at all, so a plate that was cut correctly to its own subject can still arrive with the subject cut by the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it and care does not help, because both failures present as ordinary success in every response and the frame's true text capacity depends on an applied face and size that a retired designer set and that no tool reports. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a card carrying a name and one line, and the acceptance lines about lines in full at trim and a whole subject on the framed page are the family's own standards rather than warnings. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to change what is bound and how, shortening nothing and instead re-cutting plates to the frame's own proportion and taking the long lines back to the sister for her own shorter wording.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Open and read every rendered card at trim against the normalised list, string by string, rather than judging thumbnails. For each line that stops short, do not shorten the sister's words: take them back to the family for their own decision, and meanwhile re-cut every plate destined for the framed page to that graphic frame's own proportion driven by a selection bbox on the subject, re-merge, re-render at print resolution, and read the pages again.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Sixty keepsake cards handed to mourners at the door, several of them carrying a sentence about how that person knew Walter Fernwood that stops mid phrase at the paper's edge, beside a framed A4 page on which his head is cropped by the plate frame, discovered at the service.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the importer actually did to the book's plate construct. The obvious way to give a heritage keepsake its feel is to lay each plate as a mounted print: a soft aged paper texture over the ground, a gently softened plate edge, and a two layer shadow that lifts the plate off the page. All of it exports without a single warning. What comes back is not what was authored: the blend that made the paper texture sit in the page is gone and the texture element arrives as an opaque slab, the softened edge arrives hard, and only the first shadow layer survives, so the plate reads as a flat cut out card. None of this is visible in the rendered preview either, because the preview returns the first root only and the plate pages are pages three onward. The returned markup is the only channel through which any of it can be known.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: Ordering cannot dodge it, because the construct has to be authored and exported before its normalisation exists to be read, and the preview cannot reach the pages where it lives. Nothing states it: the brief asks for a dignified book and never mentions textures, edges or shadows, and the acceptance line about the book reading as one calm is the family's own standard. It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is to rebuild the plate treatment out of different materials, which pushes work back into the imaging surface rather than re-exporting the same document.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read the returned markup root by root against what was authored, and rebuild everything that did not survive using means that do: carry the paper feel as a tinted ground and as grain applied to the plate itself in the imaging surface before it is inlined, replace the softened edge with a plate that was cut with its own margin, reduce the lift to the single shadow that survives, then re-author, re-run the readiness check and re-export, and reconcile the markup again page by page.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A memory book whose plate pages, from page three to the colophon, carry an opaque grey slab across the photographs where an aged paper texture was intended, delivered to a family five weeks after a death and printed for a service they cannot rerun.

deliverables.name: Fernwood plate set, twenty six scans across four eras plus one licensed cover frame
deliverables.spec: Every usable scan brought to one printable house look (one black point, one sense of warmth, one weight of print) with a deliberate era level decision recorded where a run could not be brought to the set, plus the postcard reverses raised to legibility while still reading as cream card and paired to their fronts, plus one licensed camera scale cover frame graded into the same world. Damage handled by crop, plate scale and placement rather than invented away, every output at or below its source dimensions, with a per era treatment log and one line on why each era differs. One set with one look, not one scan at several sizes.

deliverables.name: Service print run, keepsake cards plus the framed A4 memorial page
deliverables.spec: One A6 keepsake card per household attending, in list order, each binding the name and the sister's relationship line in full at trim plus that family branch's plate, accompanied by the A4 framed memorial page rendered as a single record at true print resolution with the plate placed so the subject is whole. Produced by reverse engineering the funeral home's two 2019 press files into live merge templates so the new pieces sit with the mother's on the shelf, with the templates and a written record of what each press file turned out to be as part of the handover.

deliverables.name: Memory book and keepsake share card as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable document carrying the book at its page canvas plus the square share card at its own: a contents page, plate pages pairing each postcard front with its reverse and the family's transcription, single plate pages for the studio and colour eras, a eulogy spread carrying the granddaughter's emphasis as real inline runs, and a colophon. Live editable text in one licensed type system at the correct numeric weight per family, every plate carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, and one unbroken calm from the contents page to the colophon. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from.

deliverables.name: Type and grid basis, handover note and shared family board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording the treatment applied per era with one line on why that era differs and exactly where damage was handled by crop or placement rather than removed, the type and grid basis by role with family, foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight used, what each 2019 press file turned out to be as editable structure and which frames could carry what, every guest list row questioned and how it was resolved, and every resize any tool reported. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the final plates and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped, so three households can see the same set.

verifiers_auto.how: Compare every delivered file's dimensions against its source per the manifest and diff the captured tradeoffs objects against the written note.

decision_gates: Which deliverables go to the merge surface and which to authored canvases, given that the family wants the printed pieces to match 2019 and the book to stay editable.
Whether damage sits inside the picture or in the margin, and therefore whether a crop is a lawful remedy or a placement decision is the only honest answer.
What to do with the four files that are photographs of framed prints rather than scans, carrying reflection and keystone that no tool here removes.
How far to carry the 1968 run toward the house neutral before the correction stops being a correction, and what the deliberate alternative is if it will not come.
Whether the postcard reverses are treated as pictures or as documents, and how legibility is bought without turning cream card grey.
Which plates the 1200 px scans can carry, and what the book grid gives up because of it.
Which guest list rows collapse onto one card, which is a family convention rather than a data rule, and how to say so rather than deciding silently.
What to do about a relationship line that will not fit, when shortening the sister's words is not the agent's call to make.
Whether to trust the mapping tool's readout of the funeral home's own text or to reconstruct the story independently from the exported document.
Whether a success message counts as verification, when nothing instructs the agent to re-export the prepared template and search for its own placeholders.
How the heritage feel is built, given that the obvious means do not survive the import and the surviving means live one surface away.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged by mourners aged 45 to 75 reading a printed page at a service.
Whether a licensed cover frame belongs on this book at all, or whether the name alone on a plain ground is the more honest cover.
why_not_vlm: Paste this brief and this shoebox into a frontier image model and it returns beautiful restored photographs. IDENTITY: these are Walter Fernwood's actual family, his father's actual hand on the back of an actual postcard, and a regenerated face or a rebuilt torn corner is a fabrication of a dead man's life presented to the people who are burying him. The client says it outright: do not invent anything that is not in the photographs. SPEC: the family needs one A6 keepsake card per household bound to the sister's own words in full at trim, matching a 2019 press file so the two pieces sit together on a shelf, plus an A4 framed page at true print resolution with the subject whole. EDITABILITY: the book is defined by being editable, because captions change until the day before the service and there is no time and no money for a redo. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did this placeholder get created, does this line reach the end of the sister's sentence at trim, did this era actually arrive beside the others, did the page that cannot be previewed survive the import.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface, and the commission is scoped so that nothing depends on the heal, clone, inpaint, sharpen or object removal the connector does not have. MERGE SPINE: building a merge template from a bare press PDF end to end headlessly is verified (convert to native, export interchange, generate mapping, prepare template, with every field confirmed present by unzipping the round trip). One record per page is confirmed for the PDF branch, single record output by recordRange is confirmed, per row image binding through an at prefixed column plus an image map keyed to bare filenames is confirmed visually, and true 300 DPI at trim is confirmed through the render tool while the merge tool's own resolution parameter is confirmed to be silently ignored. The card checkpoint rests on documented frame behaviour from a converted press PDF, whose frame granularity, bounds and applied typography are properties of the source document that no tool reports in advance, and on the verified fact that convenience readouts of story text are lossy so offsets must be reconstructed from the exported interchange file. IMAGING: straighten, adjustments masked and unmasked, dark and light portion recovery, temperature, HSL within its verified moderate range, auto tone, monochromatic tint, grain, select by prompt with returnBbox, invert, fill area, crop to bounds and crop and resize with its tradeoffs are all verified headless. The era checkpoint rests on the verified finding that HSL range holds at moderate and that a near complementary swing is out of reach, so a shifted emulsion genuinely may not converge. EXPRESS: multi page and mixed canvas in one export, true absolute unit canvases, rich inline runs surviving inside one text frame, and a genuinely editable document are verified; the checkpoint on the plate construct rests on four separately verified silent drops, mix-blend-mode dropped to an opaque shape, filter blur dropped to a hard edge, multi layer box-shadow hard truncated to layer one, and the rendition preview returning PAGE 1 ONLY so later pages are knowable from the returned markup alone. FONTS: recommend once per role, mandatory style inventory for the non standard numeric weight, display cuts reached by slug rather than weight, name laundering before the kit, and the returned slug in the CSS, all verified. STOCK and BOARDS: short queries, contentType only and orientation never passed, licence and full resolution download verified, board creation and placement verified with a twelve per call cap where 201 means partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no generative fill or object removal, no compositing, no OCR (the family supplies its own transcriptions), no bleed or press preset gate, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
